prompt:
A small wooden stage at night with a painted backdrop of a crescent moon and stars: an empty rope cot floats in mid-air under a single spotlight, a silk cloth slipping off it, smoke from a brass brazier, rows of empty folding chairs in the dark. Painted like a 1960s Indian chromolithograph print for a travelling jadoo show: hand-painted gouache with soft airbrushed glows, saturated vermilion and magenta against a deep indigo night, emerald and old-gold highlights, bold dark outlines, dramatic and mysterious, a little faded, paper grain. Wide panoramic composition: the main subject sits in the left third of the frame. Towards the right the same scene carries on, quieter and darker: open sky, distance and shadow, nothing important there, one continuous picture with no panels and no split. Full-bleed edge to edge, no border, no frame, no people, no faces, no hands. No text, no letters, no numbers, no words, no logos, no badges, no religious symbols, no writing anywhere.
